annotation.title_clean: Guidance for Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Applications (Draft Memorandum)
annotation.title_en: Guidance for Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Applications (Draft Memorandum)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Executive Office of the President
annotation.summary_en: Draft OMB memorandum implementing Executive Order 13859, guiding US federal agencies on regulating private-sector AI applications. It stresses innovation, avoiding precautionary overregulation, cost-benefit analysis, risk-based approaches, public trust, and reliance on voluntary consensus standards. It excludes government AI use and includes an agency plan template.
key_provisions_or_claims: Agencies must avoid regulatory or non-regulatory actions that needlessly hamper AI innovation and growth.
Agencies should avoid a precautionary approach and weigh AI's benefits and costs against the systems it replaces.
Ten principles for AI stewardship, including public trust, public participation, risk assessment and management, and transparency.
Agencies should consider forgoing regulation and rely on voluntary consensus standards and private-sector conformity assessment.
Agencies must submit plans identifying statutory authorities, regulatory barriers and planned actions concerning AI.
